newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen marginally weaker, stocks down.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen marginally weaker, stocks down.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were expected to soften with crude and swaps but only marginally as supplies remained tight in Singapore, traders said.
Singapore September swaps were talked lower at $109/$109.75 from Wednesday's $110.50/$115.50.
But weekly residue stocks in Singapore in the week ended September 4, fell by 246,000 barrels to 8.8 million barrels, the lowest since mid-July according to Trade Development Board figures.
"No cargoes are coming over from the Gulf," said a trader with a major oil company. "Hot weather has increased demand and prices there are too high to work cargoes to the East."
Traders said 180 cst cargoes in the Gulf were talked at a high of $7 per tonne over Mideast quotes.
But traders in Singapore remained cautious and said they would wait to seek further direction as regional demand at the same time was weak.

They said other than India's two tenders which close on Wednesday and Thursday to buy a total of 75,000 tonnes of 180 cst fuel oil, the only other regional buyer was China which was indicating at very low levels of $115-$116 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis to south China in the second half of September.
But high freight cost, due to high bunker prices, is preventing cargoes from working into China, traders said.
